description: Five optical micrographs, labelled (a)-(e), of hot-rolled AIM Fe-7 wt.% Al plates with increasing carbon content, all rendered at the same magnification; only (e) carries a white scale bar reading 250 µm. (a) 0.012 wt.% C: coarse equiaxed single-phase grains with only isolated dark dots/pits and no resolvable precipitates. (b) 0.15 wt.% C: equiaxed grains with fine dark speckles inside the grains, boundaries largely clean. (c) 0.35 wt.% C: dark precipitates form semi-continuous stringers along grain boundaries plus additional intragranular particles; grains begin to elongate. (d) 0.5 wt.% C: dense, banded dark precipitate aligned along the rolling direction. (e) 1.0 wt.% C: highest precipitate density — bright lenticular/needle-shaped and rounded particles in a darker matrix. Taken together the panels demonstrate that the precipitate volume fraction rises strongly with carbon: absent at 0.012 wt.% C, intragranular speckles at 0.15 wt.%, boundary-decorating stringers at 0.35 wt.%, banded at 0.5 wt.% and a dense network at 1.0 wt.% C. The micrographs alone do not identify the precipitate phase; the caption and citing text attribute the precipitates to Fe3AlC0.5, confirmed by XRD (Fig. 6).

observations.observation: The group is five greyscale optical micrographs labelled (a) to (e); only panel (e) contains a white scale bar annotated 250 µm, implying all panels share one magnification.
Panel (a) shows coarse equiaxed single-phase grains with clean grain boundaries and only isolated dark dots/pits; no precipitate particles are resolvable.
Panel (b) shows fine dark speckled precipitates distributed inside equiaxed grains while the grain boundaries remain largely precipitate-free.
Panel (c) shows dark precipitates decorating the grain boundaries as semi-continuous stringers, together with additional intragranular dark particles.
Panel (d) shows dark precipitate aligned in bands approximately parallel to the rolling direction.
Panel (e) shows the highest precipitate density, with bright lenticular/needle-shaped and rounded particles dispersed in a darker matrix.
Visual precipitate content increases monotonically from panel (a) to panel (e) as the labelled carbon content rises.
The caption states the panels are optical micrographs of hot-rolled AIM Fe-7 wt.% Al plates containing (a) 0.012 wt.% C, (b) 0.15 wt.% C, (c) 0.35 wt.% C, (d) 0.5 wt.% C and (e) 1.0 wt.% C.
The citing text refers to the alloy of Fig. 5 as '0.02 C', whereas the caption labels the corresponding lowest-carbon panel as 0.012 wt.% C; the two labels disagree.
The citing text states the low-carbon alloy (Fig. 5) showed a single-phase structure with no precipitates, matching the appearance of panel (a).
The citing text states the precipitates seen at higher carbon levels were confirmed to be Fe3AlC0.5 by X-ray diffraction analysis (Fig. 6, Philips 3710 diffractometer).
The citing text states the volume fraction of precipitates increases significantly with increasing carbon content, which is the trend visible across panels (a)-(e).
The citing text states the ingots were hot forged and hot rolled to 12 mm thickness, the processing condition behind the rolled/banded microstructures shown.

subfigures.description: Optical micrograph of the 0.012 wt.% C plate: coarse equiaxed grains, clean boundaries, only a few isolated dark dots/pits; no resolvable precipitates.
Optical micrograph of the 0.15 wt.% C plate: equiaxed grains filled with fine dark speckled precipitates, grain boundaries largely free of precipitate.
Optical micrograph of the 0.35 wt.% C plate: dark precipitates outline grain boundaries as semi-continuous stringers, with further dark particles inside the grains and slightly elongated grains.
Optical micrograph of the 0.5 wt.% C plate: strongly banded structure of dark aligned precipitate parallel to the rolling direction.

Optical micrograph of the 1.0 wt.% C plate: highest precipitate density, bright lenticular/needle-shaped and rounded particles dispersed in a darker grey matrix; contains the white scale bar labelled 250 µm.

unreadable_items: The precipitate phase cannot be identified from the optical micrographs themselves; identification (Fe3AlC0.5) comes only from the citing text/XRD reference, and the phase formula is garbled in the citing text as 'Fi e3AlC0.5'
No grain-size, precipitate-size or volume-fraction values are printed on any panel
Scale bar is present only in panel (e); magnification of panels (a)-(d) is inferred, not printed
Etchant and polishing details are not visible in the images
